2. If it was logged as a request, twenty working days from 24 September ended on 22 October 2026 (FOIA section 10(1); EIR regulation 5(2)). Please ask the department to respond for Cadw's own holdings, or to say when it will.

This is separate from my complaint to Mr Wigley (TO/HF/05677/26) and from ATISN 26-0009 and 26-0010, which stay in their own threads.

Kind regards,

Requester

texts.gm-1a1a1c17e5eadd4b:
Dear Information Commissioner's Office,

Further to my email earlier today asking for more time (same thread, internal review outcome attached), please treat this email as my formal complaint under section 50 of the Freedom of Information Act 2000 about Amgueddfa Cymru – Museum Wales's handling of my request FOI 2026-024.

An extension of time is still my preference, so that I can send a fuller complaint. If you cannot grant one, please rely on this email as my complaint, made within six weeks of the internal review outcome of 22 September 2026.

Request: on 27 July 2026 I asked for recorded information about a discovery at Great House Farm (Tŷ Mawr), Llandough-juxta-Penarth, near Cardiff (Heneb HER GGAT02038s; RCAHMW NPRN 20182). A published local history account records that a soldier's remains and his horse were found beneath the dining-room floor, that the remains were reburied in the churchyard, and that the visor and lance were given to the National Museum of Wales. I asked for accession, donation or transfer records, accession numbers and provenance notes, catalogue entries and correspondence, records of the associated remains, and any discovery or excavation reports.

Response: on 25 August 2026, one working day after the 20-working-day limit, the Museum said under section 1(1)(a) that it held no information. It also said its searches had found records of "other archaeological discoveries recorded at Great House Farm (Ty Mawr), Llandough", and that it had treated those as outside the request without describing them.

Internal review: I asked for a review on 26 August 2026. My point was that the searches were framed too narrowly around a "medieval visor, lance, helmet or other item of armour", and that the original find may have been described differently (for example as Roman). The review, issued on 22 September 2026, upheld the "not held" answer. It also said that those other records would receive "a separate response". I have not identified a response in which the Museum disclosed or described the records it set aside.

Why I believe the "not held" answer and its scope are doubtful:
1. The Museum confirms it holds records of archaeological discoveries at the same farm, yet it judged them unrelated without telling me what they are, so I cannot test that judgement. Whether they relate to the reported discovery is the question I asked.
2. Nomenclature is a major cause of confusion for all parties, and I ask the Commissioner and the Museum to take it into account. The same property appears in records as Great House Farm, Great House, Greathouse, Tŷ Mawr, Ty Mawr Farm, Tymawr, Cydfin Farm and Llandough Home Farm (1881 census). The place appears as Llandough, Llandough-juxta-Penarth, Llandough near Penarth and Llandough near Cardiff, and it is easily confused with Llandow in the Vale of Glamorgan. The Museum's own records use further terms: "Church Farm / Llandough Church Farm" in the provenance of accession 63.24 (medieval ironwork found about 1858), and "Llandough Farm (opposite hospital)", which is a separate farmstead. A search under one name or a modern object term can miss a record catalogued under another. I ask that the searches be repeated across all of these names, and across the donor names, periods and object descriptions a nineteenth-century accession might carry.
3. The reply was late (25 August against a due date of 24 August).

I ask the Commissioner to decide:
(a) whether, on the balance of probabilities, the Museum holds information within the scope of my request, including the records it set aside as "other discoveries" at Great House Farm and any record linked to accession 63.24;
(b) whether its searches were adequate, and to ask it to explain the search terms, name variants, systems and date ranges it used;
(c) that the Museum breached section 10(1) by replying late; and
(d) that the Museum should issue a fresh response covering the records it set aside.

The research behind this complaint, including the full name-variation index, is published at https://bucklerfamily.estate, and all ongoing research will continue to be published there.

The internal review outcome is attached. I can supply the original request (27 July), the Museum's response (25 August) and my review request (26 August) on request.

Yours faithfully,
Requester 
[email redacted]

Thank you for contacting the Information Commissioner’s Office. We confirm that we have received your correspondence. If you have any special requirements that mean you would like us to communicate with you in a specific way, please let us know and we will make adjustments if we can.
If you have made a new complaint - we’re unlikely to look into it unless you have raised it with the responsible organisation (for a data protection complaint) or the responsible public authority (for a freedom of information complaint) first. Please make sure you have sent us a copy of their final response to you. We're supporting a high number of people with their complaints at the moment. For the latest timescales to allocate cases, please visit the make a complaint page<https://ico.org.uk/make-a-complaint/data-protection-complaints/> on our website. We apologise for this delay but we want to reassure you we take your complaint very seriously.
If your correspondence relates to an existing case - we will add it to your case and consider it on allocation to a case officer. If you believe we have either failed to take appropriate steps to respond to your data protection complaint, or we do not provide you with information about the progress or outcome of your complaint within the next three months, you may be able to apply to the First-tier Tribunal to require us to respond to your complaint or to provide you with information about its progress. (www.gov.uk<http://www.gov.uk/> - information rights and data protection: appeal against the Information Commissioner)
If you have asked us for advice - we will respond within 7 days. While you wait, you should regularly check our website (www.ico.org.uk<http://www.ico.org.uk/>) for relevant guidance, as we are updating this all the time. You should read our Guide to the UK GDPR<https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/guide-to-data-protection/guide-to-the-general-data-protection-regulation-gdpr/>. If you have raised a question that we have answered on our website, we may respond by sending you a link to it. But will do our best to provide you with the information you need.
If you represent an organisation and you are reporting a personal data breach under the GDPR or the Data Protection Act 2018 - we aim to contact you within seven days to confirm receipt and to provide you with a case reference number. If you want advice urgently, you should telephone our helpline on [phone redacted]. You can find out more about data breach reporting on our website.
Where a significant cyber incident occurs, you may also need to report this to the National Cyber Security Centre (the NCSC). To help you decide, you should read the NCSC’s guidance about their role and the type of incidents that you should consider reporting. (www.ncsc.gov.uk<http://www.ncsc.gov.uk/> -incident-management)
Incidents that might lead to a heightened risk of individuals being affected by fraud, should be reported to Report Fraud (https://www.reportfraud.police.uk/) - the UK’s national fraud and cybercrime reporting centre. If your organisation is in Scotland, then reports should be made to Police Scotland (www.scotland.police.uk<http://www.scotland.police.uk/>).
If you are a Communications Service Provider reporting a security breach under the Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations – you will need to report the security breach via the secure portal that can be found on the PECR pages of our website.
If you represent an organisation and are reporting a potential incident under the NIS Directive - we will contact you as soon as we can. You can find out more about the NIS Regulations on our website
If you represent an organisation and you are reporting a security breach within the definition of the eIDAS regulation – we will contact you as soon as we can. You can find out more about the eIDAS regulation on our website.
If you have reported spam email – we are unlikely to need to contact you again, unless we need more information to help with our investigations. We publish details about the action we've taken on nuisance messages on our website.
If you have asked for information you think we might hold - we will contact you if we need any more information to help us respond. Otherwise, we will respond within our public and statutory service levels. For more information please visit our webpage ‘request information from us’ (go to our homepage and follow the link for ‘about the ICO’ and ‘our information’).
If you have only copied your correspondence to us - we will not respond.
There is more detailed information, including information on our current response times, on our service standards and what to expect webpage. You can also call [phone redacted], we welcome calls in Welsh on [phone redacted]. You can also contact us on live chat (please visit our webpage ‘contact us’ and ‘live chat’).
For information about what we do with personal data please see our privacy notice: https://ico.org.uk/global/privacy-notice/
Yours sincerely
The Information Commissioner’s Office

Thank you for your reply of 2 November 2026, which identifies Western Ground Rents Limited as company 00342092 (incorporated 2 July 1938, dissolved 22 August 1997) and Mountjoy Limited as company 00179977 (incorporated 27 February 1922, dissolved 31 January 2001). This email is not an order for any documents.

That is a general statement. It does not say what happened to the records of these two companies. Please answer each of the following as held or not held:

My emails of 29 and 31 October set out my other questions, including those on Mountjoy Limited's records and the 1926 and 1938 conveyances. I would be grateful for an answer to each of them that you can give.

Yours faithfully,

Requester
